mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: In the 20-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05), or the Fed raises rates within 3 months and reverses the trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as labor market expansion supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month and HOUST rises by > 5% month-over-month
regime_hint: Expanding labor market with rising consumer sentiment
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are negative or flat, and either PAYEMS or HOUST shows no meaningful correlation with SPX returns in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy via GDPC1 ) of at least 4% for two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as it signals resilient consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥ 4% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: Stable or improving consumer demand cycle
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative, and GDPC1 does not sustain the required growth pattern in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 5% in a month followed by a rebound of > 8% in the next month predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as it reflects a cyclical supply-side release.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% then rises by > 8% in the following month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative during the rebound window, or the pattern does not repeat in subsequent cycles.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 60-day forward returns as the market anticipates further rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for 3 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 3% over the same period
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over 60 days are negative, or inflation rises while unemployment remains low.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (RSAFS) accompanied by a sustained rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) over two months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as it signals labor market cooling and wage moderation.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by > 10% month-over-month while PAYEMS increases by > 2% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market cooling with rising employment
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative in the test window, or the labor indicators revert in the opposite direction.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggests disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as investors anticipate rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during the 5-day window despite CPIAUCSL remaining below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a prolonged period of stagnation (≥ 3 consecutive months at or below the prior month's level) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as it indicates weak economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% then remains flat or declines for ≥ 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the stagnation window, or INDPRO rebounds sharply within 3 months.
